row.notes: Inner-tree bracket search of the 2-D tyre curve sets: each outer node's value at +0x28 is a std::map<float,...> with head value+8, size value+0x10; node left +0, parent +8, right +0x10, isnil byte +0x19, key float +0x20. Writes the lower and upper node to bracket[0] and bracket[1]; void (every caller reads the pair from the stack and overwrites rax). Size 1: both begin. begin.key > key (vucomiss 0x142e7c1ea; ja): both begin. Walks size-1 steps to the last node; key > last.key (vucomiss 0x142e7c253; ja): both last. Otherwise upper = upper_bound over [begin, last), so at most last (key == last.key gives last and its predecessor) that goes left on jb (0x142e7c304), lower = its predecessor (MSVC tree decrement, 0x142e7c3b1-0x142e7c40d). With two or more nodes, a NaN key fails both ja tests and takes jb at every compare (unordered sets CF), so upper = begin and lower = the predecessor of begin, which is the tree's head (isnil 1, value never constructed); a number or an infinity always brackets two real nodes. Ghidra prints the two range tests as param_2 < key and param_2 <= key, which hides the unordered case; the disassembly is the reference. Leaf: no calls, no RIP-relative operands, first instructions push rsi / mov rax,[rcx+8] (5 bytes). Same instruction stream as Car_Tyre_CurveMap_FindBracketB apart from the container offsets, and the same stream on Steam 26566308 0x142e7e750 and EA 1.0.145 0x142e72350 (branch targets masked). callers: census steam 0x2e7c1c0 (Car_Tyre_SampleCurveSet2KeyLerp 0x142e7c077/0x142e7c0f9, Car_Tyre_SampleWearCurve2DAlt 0x142e7c6ac/0x142e7c72e). Core's tyre curve guard wraps it and passes the lowest float for a NaN key.

V120001 Blind re-derivation on d873a1c8. Leaf in .xtls, .pdata 0x142e7c1c0-0x142e7c40f. The instruction stream is identical to 0x142e7bd50 (168 instructions, same relative branch targets) except the 4 container loads: head [rcx+8] at 0x142e7c1c1/0x142e7c1cb/0x142e7c25e, size [rcx+0x10] at 0x142e7c1d6. Args rcx/xmm1/r8 as in B; rax is garbage at ret and the callers ignore it (the next instruction loads from the stack, then calls 0x142e7c410/0x142e7c800 with no rax read), so void. rcx at every call is lea [outer_node+0x28] (0x142e7c054, 0x142e7c081, 0x142e7c0db, 0x142e7c689, 0x142e7c710), the mapped value of the outer map. The callers read its head at node+0x30 and size at node+0x38 (0x142e7bfe3), which agrees with head +8 and size +0x10. Key compares: vucomiss begin.key,key at 0x142e7c1ea + ja (both begin); vucomiss key,last.key at 0x142e7c253 + ja (both last); jb left at 0x142e7c304 in the upper_bound over [begin,last); predecessor 0x142e7c3b5-0x142e7c40d. NaN: both ja fall through on unordered and jb is taken at every compare, which gives upper=begin and lower=--begin=head (isnil). A number or infinity always brackets two real nodes. Same imprecisions as B: NaN->head needs size>=2 (je 0x142e7c1de returns begin twice when size is 1); key==last.key gives upper=last, not end(); size 0 is outside the contract. The samplers check only the first outer node's inner size (0x142e7bfe3/0x142e7c633), not the inner sizes of the lower and upper nodes passed here. Callers (census steam 0x2e7c1c0): 0x142e7c077 and 0x142e7c0f9 in 0x142e7bfa0, 0x142e7c6ac and 0x142e7c72e in 0x142e7c5f0; 0 thunks, 0 jumps, 0 lea, 0 pointers. Steam 26566308 0x142e7e750 and EA 1.0.145 0x142e72350 have the same stream, and their callers sit at the same sampler offsets. Blindness caveat: my record dump printed the row's notes field before I derived anything (I filtered only the top-level notes key); every fact below I re-derived from the disassembly and the census myself.
